tasks.title: Render heading lines inside blockquote/list content as real headings (guide-book pp. 41, 43, 47)
tasks.prompt:
You are implementing the single fix task of the M1 sign-off round for the SXC-1 Trainer.
Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1. Everything is committed at 66ddfb8 and green; this is a
targeted correctness fix found by the Opus sign-off review, not a rework.

YOU OWN EXACTLY THESE THREE FILES:

    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/src/SXC1/Content/Markdown.hs
    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/app/View/Blocks.hs
    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/site/test/CheckContent.hs

Touch nothing else. In particular do NOT change site/src/SXC1/Content/Stats.hs,
site/src/SXC1/Content/Outline.hs, scripts/check-site.sh or scripts/browser-check.mjs.

THE DEFECT
Three heading lines inside the guide book's "Tip" callout blockquotes render to the reader
as literal hash marks:

    guide-book p.41   "### Use the two input styles for different situations"
    guide-book p.43   "### When you want to practice before inputting"
    guide-book p.47   "### Looped sounds sync to the sequence tempo!"

Source lines 1284, 1334 and 1452 of translations/guide-book.md, each of the form
`> ### <text>` inside a `> **Tip (character callout):**` blockquote. Verified in the real
browser: the rendered DOM contains the characters `###` as body text.

ROOT CAUSE
`parseBlocksEngine :: Int -> Bool -> [Text] -> [Text] -> ([Block], [Text])` in Markdown.hs
takes an `allowHeadings` flag and is called with `False` for blockquote content and
list-item children, so a de-quoted heading line falls through to the paragraph rule and its
`#` characters survive as text.

WHY THE STATED JUSTIFICATION IS WRONG
The in-source comment says disabling headings in nested content "is also what keeps the
golden `headings` count exact". That is not so, and I verified it: `countHeadingLines` runs
`headingLineOf` over raw `T.lines`, and `headingLineOf` requires the line to BEGIN with `#`.
A `> ### ...` line begins with `>`, so it is already excluded. Counting the raw
`^#{1,6} +\S` lines of translations/guide-book.md yields exactly 188 — the golden — whether
or not nested headings are recognised. The flag buys nothing and costs rendering fidelity.
briefs/M1-plan.md 4.5 specifies the blockquote rule as "strip the marker and recursively
parse the remainder as blocks", which includes headings.

THE COUPLING YOU MUST RESPECT (this is why the fix is not a one-character change)
`mkDoc` pre-computes the per-page anchor-slug supply from ONLY the top-level headings:

    perPageHeads = [ (n, mapMaybe headingLineOf ls) | (n, ls) <- pages0 ]
    dedupedSlugs = dedupeSlugs (map (slugify . snd) flatHeads)
    slugsByPage  = regroup (map (length . snd) perPageHeads) dedupedSlugs

and every top-level `Heading` consumes one slug via `popSlug`. If nested headings start
consuming from that same supply, every subsequent heading on pages 41, 43 and 47 gets the
WRONG anchor (and the supply can run dry). Do not let that happen.

WHAT TO DO
1. Markdown.hs: make nested (blockquote / list-child) content recognise heading lines and
   emit real `Heading` blocks. Nested headings are NOT outline targets and MUST NOT consume
   from the page's anchor-slug supply. Give them an empty anchor (`""`) — or a separately
   derived one — but keep the top-level supply untouched and consumed in exactly the same
   order as today.
2. View/Blocks.hs: when a `Heading`'s anchor is empty, render the heading element WITHOUT
   an `id` attribute (a real `h3`/`h4`, styled by the existing `.md-note h3` / `.page-body
   h1..h6` rules — reader-styles already styles headings generically, so no CSS change is
   needed and you do not own index.html anyway). Clamp the level exactly as today.
3. CheckContent.hs: add regression assertions under a new label, keeping all existing ones:
   a. For each document, count `Heading` blocks that occur nested inside `Quote` or list-item
      children (use the existing `flattenBlocks` helper minus the top level). Assert
      guide-book == 3 and startup-guide/midi/oss == 0.
   b. A general literal-hash guard: assert that no `Str` inline anywhere in the corpus
      (top-level or nested, including table cells and list items) begins with one to six `#`
      characters followed by a space. This catches this whole class of regression, not just
      the three known lines.
   c. Assert that the guide-book anchors on pages 41, 43 and 47 are unchanged (see the
      byte-exact list below).

INVARIANTS THAT MUST NOT MOVE (all verified green at 66ddfb8 before your change)
  * Golden stats, all four documents, unchanged:
        headings    188 / 51 / 8 / 6
        sections     29 / 21 / 6 / 5
        subsections  78 / 27 / 1 / 0
        parts         5 /  0 / 0 / 0
        chars    111559 / 29145 / 7372 / 42533
  * The golden 7-group guide-book outline and its five part titles are unchanged.
  * `exe:content-check` still passes every pre-existing assertion (it was 230/230; it will be
    230 + your new ones).
  * `./scripts/check-site.sh` still passes (it was 37/37) including the three-way agreement.
  * `node scripts/browser-check.mjs` still passes (it was 25/25).
  * These top-level anchors must remain byte-identical:
        p.41  h-try-creating-various-drum-patterns, h-example-1-dance-beat,
              h-example-2-16-beat, h-example-3-half-time
        p.43  h-try-creating-a-pattern-that-includes-non-drum-sounds-too
        p.47  h-try-layering-pad-performance-over-sequence-playback

DONE LOOKS LIKE
  * `. "$HOME/.ghc-wasm/env"; cd /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1; ./scripts/build-site.sh` succeeds, -Wall clean.
  * The rendered DOM for guide-book pp. 41, 43 and 47 contains ZERO occurrences of `###`,
    and each of the three Tip callouts shows a real heading element. Verify in a browser:
        ./scripts/serve-site.sh --port 8321 &
        google-chrome --headless=new --disable-gpu --no-sandbox \
          --user-data-dir=$(mktemp -d) --virtual-time-budget=9000 --dump-dom \
          'http://127.0.0.1:8321/#/m/guide-book/p/41' | grep -c '###'
    Paste the before/after counts into your report.
  * `./scripts/check-site.sh` exits 0 and content-check reports its new total.
  * NEGATIVE CONTROL you must perform and report: temporarily revert your Markdown.hs change,
    rebuild, and confirm your new CheckContent.hs assertion (b) FAILS — then restore. An
    assertion that cannot fail is worthless.
  * Report the anchor lists for pp. 41, 43, 47 after the change, to prove they did not move.

acceptance_checks: Heading lines inside blockquote and list-item content are parsed as real Heading blocks; the rendered DOM for guide-book pp. 41, 43 and 47 contains zero literal '###' and each Tip callout shows a heading element.

Nested headings do not consume the page's pre-computed anchor-slug supply: the top-level anchors on pp. 41, 43 and 47 are byte-identical to those at 66ddfb8 (h-try-creating-various-drum-patterns, h-example-1-dance-beat, h-example-2-16-beat, h-example-3-half-time, h-try-creating-a-pattern-that-includes-non-drum-sounds-too, h-try-layering-pad-performance-over-sequence-playback).
View/Blocks.hs omits the id attribute when a Heading's anchor is empty and still clamps the level to 1..4; no CSS change was required or made.

CheckContent.hs gains: a nested-Heading count assertion (guide-book 3, others 0), a general guard that no Str inline anywhere begins with 1-6 '#' followed by a space, and an assertion pinning the pp. 41/43/47 anchors.
All golden statistics are unchanged (chars/pages/headings/sections/subsections/parts for all four documents) and the golden 7-group outline with its five part titles still reproduces.
./scripts/build-site.sh is -Wall clean, exe:content-check passes all pre-existing assertions plus the new ones, ./scripts/check-site.sh exits 0, and scripts/browser-check.mjs still passes.

No file outside the three owned paths was modified.
